title: Plural 8: All Six Cases Together
description: A mixed review of the regular plural endings across all six cases (lessons 1-7). Pick the right plural form for the job, name the case at work, and produce a few forms yourself. No new material.
descriptionRussian: Повторение регулярных окончаний множественного числа во всех шести падежах (уроки 1-7). Выберите нужную форму, определите падеж и образуйте несколько форм самостоятельно. Ничего нового.
intro: All six cases at once, and by now the decision tree is short. Is it the genitive, which needs a gender check and possibly a vanished vowel? Is it the accusative, where you ask whether the noun is alive? Or is it one of the three that take a single ending regardless. Three of the six are that last kind.
rules: Plural nominative (L1): hard stems → -ы (журналы, машины), soft → -и (словари, песни), neuter → -а / -я (окна, моря). Four endings, picked by gender and hard / soft.
Plural accusative (L2): inanimate plural acc = pl nom (читает книги); animate plural acc = pl gen (знает друзей). Animacy split applies to ALL three genders in the plural.

Plural genitive (L3 + L4): masc -ов / -ев / -ей (журналов, музеев, учителей, врачей); fem -а / hard neuter -о → zero ending (книг, окон), soft fem / soft neuter → -ей (тетрадей, морей). Family-pl masc splits two ways: -ьев for брат / стул (братьев, стульев), -ей for друг / сын (друзей, сыновей).
Plural dative (L5): one ending across all three genders. Hard → -ам, soft → -ям. Family-pl → -ьям; suppletive дети / люди → детям / людям.
Plural instrumental (L6): one ending across all three genders. Hard → -ами, soft → -ями. Family-pl → -ьями; suppletive дети / люди / лошади → contracted -ьми (детьми, людьми, лошадьми).
Plural prepositional (L7): one ending across all three genders. Hard → -ах, soft → -ях. Family-pl → -ьях; suppletive дети / люди → детях / людях. Always after a preposition (в, на, о / об, при).
examples: Антон часто думает о книгах. (Anton often thinks about books.) Prepositional pl after о, hard feminine -ах: книгах.
Лена помогает студентам. (Lena helps the students.) Dative pl after помогать, hard masculine -ам: студентам.
Ольга гордится результатами. (Olga is proud of the results.) Instrumental pl, hard masculine -ами: результатами.
В офисе пять столов. (There are five desks in the office.) Genitive pl after пять, hard masculine -ов: столов.
Антон видит соседей. (Anton sees the neighbours.) Animate accusative pl copies the genitive: соседей.
В городе красивые улицы. (In the city there are beautiful streets.) Nominative pl subject, hard feminine -ы: улицы.

items.hint: Recap from L7: о + ? Hard fem with velar к, prep pl ending?
items.explanation: L7 recap: о + prepositional for the topic of speech / thought. Книга is hard fem -а with velar к; the prep pl is -ах by the spelling rule: книгах. Today's lesson mixes all six cases.

items.hint: Помогать takes the dative. Дети is suppletive; the dat pl ending goes on the suppletive stem.
items.explanation: Помогать + dat is one of the core dative triggers. Дети is the suppletive plural of ребёнок; the dat pl is детям (suppletive stem дет- + soft ending -ям). Compare детьми (instr pl, contracted -ьми) and детях (prep pl, soft -ях).

items.promptEnglish: Masha is proud of her teachers.
items.hint: Гордиться takes the instrumental directly (no preposition). Soft -ь masc + ?
items.explanation: Гордиться is one of the gerundive verbs that take the instrumental directly. Учитель is soft -ь masc, so the instr pl is -ями: учителями. Compare учителях (prep pl, after о or в) and учителям (dat pl, after помогать).

items.promptEnglish: There are five desks in the office.
items.hint: After numbers 5+, the noun is in which case? Hard masc cons + ending?
items.explanation: After numbers 5 and above, the counted noun goes into the genitive plural. Стол is hard masc cons; the gen pl ending is -ов: столов. Compare with numbers 2-4, which take the genitive singular instead (два стола).

items.hint: Знать takes the accusative. Друг is animate; animate plural acc = ?
items.explanation: Знать takes the accusative. Друг is animate, so the plural acc borrows the genitive plural form: друзей (family-pl with the -ей ending, like сыновей; compare братьев / стульев with -ьев). The animacy split applies across all three genders in the plural; compare читает книги (inanimate, acc = nom).

items.promptEnglish: In this city there are beautiful streets.
items.hint: The streets are the SUBJECT of the sentence. Subject = which case?
items.explanation: Улицы is the subject of 'есть красивые улицы' (the verb есть is implied). Subjects take the nominative. Улица is hard fem -а; the pl nom is -ы: улицы.

blanks: У Маши много _____. (Masha has many sisters.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: После много + countable plural, the noun is in the genitive plural. Сестра is fem -а with consonant cluster; the gen pl gets a stressed fleeting -ё-: сестёр.

errorCorrection.sentence: В парке Антон встретил своих братья.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In the park Anton met his brothers.
errorCorrection.explanation: Брат is animate, so its accusative plural is the genitive plural: встретил братьев. Братья is the nominative plural, fine as a subject (братья пришли) but not as the object of встретил.

errorCorrection.sentence: На полке стоит много книг и пять словарёв.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: On the shelf there are many books and five dictionaries.
errorCorrection.explanation: Словарь is a soft masculine noun (-ь), so its genitive plural is -ей: пять словарей. Словарёв is the trap of grafting the hard -ов ending onto a soft stem; it is not a real form. The number пять triggers the genitive plural, and the soft -ь supplies -ей, the same ending seen in the husher nouns ножей, врачей.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша пишет письма свои подругам каждую неделю.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha writes letters to her girlfriends every week.
errorCorrection.explanation: Подругам is the dative plural (the recipients of the letters), so the possessive must agree in the dative plural: своим подругам. Свои is the nominative or inanimate-accusative plural, the form that would modify a direct object, but here подругам is the indirect object. The verb писать sends letters TO people, so the recipient and its modifier both take the dative plural: своим подругам.

minimalPairs.explanation: Помогать takes the dative, not the genitive. Друзей is the gen pl (or the animate plural acc), used after много or as the direct object of знать / видеть. Друзьям is the dat pl with the family-pl ending -ьям.
С (with) for accompaniment takes the instrumental, not the dative. Учителями is the instr pl with the soft -ями ending. Учителям is the dat pl ('to the teachers'), which doesn't fit after с.

patternRecognition.question: What case is книг in?
patternRecognition.explanation: Много + countable plural triggers the genitive plural. Книг is the gen pl with the zero ending characteristic of hard fem -а stems (the L4 rule).

patternRecognition.question: What case is девочкам in?
patternRecognition.explanation: Помогать takes the dative (L5). Девочкам is the dative plural; the velar к keeps the ending hard, -ам.

patternRecognition.question: What case is коллегами in?
patternRecognition.explanation: С (together with) takes the instrumental (L6). Коллегами is the instrumental plural with the hard -ами ending.

patternRecognition.question: What case is соседях in?
patternRecognition.explanation: О takes the prepositional (L7). Соседях is the prepositional plural of сосед with the soft -ях ending.

reviewVocab.definition: the master plural-cases table; six cases × two columns (hard / soft) = a compact view of all twelve plural endings.
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Маша помогает братьям' слово 'братьям' стоит в дательном падеже множественного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: family-plural masculines (брат, друг, сын, стул); their plural stem takes -ья (братья), and all oblique cases use the soft ending on that stem: братьев / братьям / братьями / братьях.
reviewVocab.example: Маша часто пишет братьям, гуляет с друзьями и думает о сыновьях.

reviewVocab.definition: suppletive plurals (дети, люди, лошади); their plural stem replaces the singular entirely. The instrumental uses the contracted -ьми (детьми, людьми, лошадьми); the other cases take the regular soft endings.
reviewVocab.example: Маша помогает детям, гордится людьми и работает с лошадьми.
